summary.text: Alicia Collins is a Republican state representative from Maine who has represented District 61 since 2024 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.

paragraphs.text: Alicia Collins assumed office in the Maine House of Representatives on December 3, 2024, succeeding Richard T. Bradstreet, after winning the 2024 general election over Democrat Laura Jones.
Ballotpedia notes that, as of her 2024 campaign, she served as a selectman for the Town of Sidney, Maine.
In the 2025-2026 session she was assigned to the Leaves of Absence Committee.
She advanced from the June 9, 2026 Republican primary and faces Democrat Robin Crawley in the general election.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Collins said she has lived in Maine her whole life and described her platform as: all lives matter, freedom to exercise civil liberties, and the ability of Maine people to make their own choices.

She listed her campaign messages as controlling state spending through audits of state departments, eliminating taxes and fees to make Maine more competitive, and encouraging school districts to return to basics such as reading, writing, arithmetic, science and history.
She said Gun Owners of Maine has given her voting record an A+.
